discovery: Realization of strongly interacting Fermi gases and fermionic superfluidity across the BEC-BCS crossover

nominees.name: Rudolf Grimm
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

nominees.name: Christophe Salomon
nominees.affiliation: Laboratoire Kastler Brossel, ENS-PSL, CNRS, Paris, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / ultracold quantum gases
motivation: Using Feshbach resonances in ultracold fermionic lithium-6 and potassium, the nominees turned the long-standing theoretical idea of a continuous crossover from Bose-Einstein condensation of tightly bound molecules to BCS pairing into a controllable laboratory system. Grimm's group produced long-lived molecular condensates and measured the pairing gap and collective modes through the crossover; Salomon's group created Bose-Fermi superfluid mixtures and precisely determined the universal equation of state of the unitary Fermi gas; Ketterle's group gave definitive proof of fermionic superfluidity through vortex lattices and explored imbalanced pairing. The unitary Fermi gas they established is now a quantitative benchmark connecting atomic physics with superconductivity, neutron stars and the quark-gluon plasma. This work created a new field of strongly correlated quantum matter with tunable interactions, underpinning today's quantum simulation of fermionic many-body physics.
